title: Otto Frank Reads His Daughter's Diary
text:
In July 1942 Otto Frank, a German Jewish businessman who had moved his family to Amsterdam, took his wife and two daughters into hiding in a secret annex behind his company's offices. Four other people joined them. Office employees, among them Miep Gies, brought them food and news for more than two years. On 4 August 1944 the hiding place was discovered and all eight were arrested and deported.

Otto was the only one of the eight to survive. He was liberated at Auschwitz in January 1945 and made his way back to Amsterdam. There, in the summer of 1945, he learned that his daughters, Margot and Anne, had died in the camp of Bergen-Belsen.

After the arrest, Miep Gies had gathered up the notebooks and loose pages of Anne's diary from the floor of the annex and locked them away, hoping to return them to her. Now she gave them to Otto. He began reading, and he was overwhelmed. He later said he had not known the depth of his daughter's thoughts and feelings, and that he realized how little a parent may really know a child.

Anne had hoped to publish a book about the annex after the war, and had begun revising her diary for that purpose. Otto decided to fulfill her wish. In June 1947 the diary was published in Dutch as Het Achterhuis, The Secret Annex. Otto spent the rest of his life answering readers' letters and promoting her message.
lesson: Our children may have inner lives deeper than we imagine, so it is worth listening while we can. Honoring a loved one's wish can carry their voice far beyond their life.
people: Otto Frank, Anne Frank, Margot Frank, Miep Gies
source: Anne Frank, Het Achterhuis (1947); Miep Gies with Alison Leslie Gold, Anne Frank Remembered (1987); Anne Frank House archives
